findings.claim: "Understanding the differences between these two types is a key part of AQA and regularly tested in exams."
findings.truth: House rule: the exam board is never named in student-facing text. The sentence is also broken English - content is not 'a key part of AQA'.

findings.claim: "AQA Required Practical 3 involves investigating the effect of a range of concentrations of salt or sugar solutions on the mass of plant tissue..."
findings.truth: In this qualification the osmosis practical is Required practical activity 2. Required practical activity 3 is the food tests (Benedict's, iodine, Biuret). The number 3 comes from the separate-biology spec, which this unit is not built to.
findings.evidence: spec 4.1.3.2 'Required practical activity 2: investigate the effect of a range of concentrations of salt or sugar solutions on the mass of plant tissue'; spec 4.2.2.1 'Required practical activity 3: use qualitative reagents...'

findings.claim: "AQA Required Practical 5 asks you to investigate how pH affects the rate of amylase activity."
findings.truth: In this qualification the amylase pH practical is Required practical activity 4. Number 5 is the photosynthesis practical. The method described is otherwise right (continuous sampling, iodine every 30 seconds, temperature controlled by a water bath).

findings.truth: Board named in student-facing text.

findings.claim: Q3 mark scheme: "Alternative: rate = 1 divided by time = 1 / 4 = 0.25 per minute (if using rate = 1/t, award both marks)."
findings.truth: The question says 'Give your answer in cm3 per minute', so an answer of 0.25 per minute is in the wrong unit and cannot score both marks. The main route (10 / 4 = 2.5 cm3 per minute) recomputes correctly.
findings.evidence: recomputation: 10 / 4 = 2.5; the alternative answers a different question

findings.claim: "Carcinogens, including ionising radiation (such as UV light and X-rays), are risk factors for cancer."
findings.truth: Ultraviolet is not ionising radiation. This spec's own physics section separates the two: ultraviolet ages skin and raises skin-cancer risk, while X-rays and gamma rays are the ionising radiation that mutates genes. A student who writes 'UV is ionising' loses the mark on the physics paper. UV is already covered in this lesson as a lifestyle risk factor.
findings.evidence: spec 6.6.2.3 'Ultraviolet waves can cause skin to age prematurely and increase the risk of skin cancer. X-rays and gamma rays are ionising radiation that can cause the mutation of genes and cancer.'; spec 4.2.2.6 'Carcinogens, including ionising radiation, as risk factors in cancer'

findings.claim: Card 4: q "_____ and Disease Health is defined as a state of physical and mental well-being", a "Health".
findings.truth: A mangled auto-generated cloze card: the prompt is a heading spliced onto the first sentence, and the answer 'Health' repeats card 1's answer 'health', so the deck teaches nothing and trips the duplicate-answer rule. Rebuilt as a benign-tumour definition card from the lesson's own glossary.

findings.claim: "Required Practical 6: You must know how to investigate the effect of light intensity on the rate of photosynthesis using pondweed" (and the same number in the revision tip).
findings.truth: In this qualification the photosynthesis practical is Required practical activity 5. The method described is right. Lessons 2, 3 and 8 all carry separate-biology practical numbers (3, 5, 6) where this course uses 2, 4 and 5; only lesson 1's number 1 happens to match.
findings.evidence: spec 4.4.1.2 'Required practical activity 5: investigate the effect of light intensity on the rate of photosynthesis using an aquatic organism such as pondweed'

findings.claim: "For calculation questions on photosynthesis rate, remember that light intensity follows an inverse square relationship with distance..." (and practice Q3, which asks the student to apply 1/d squared).
findings.truth: The inverse square law is Higher tier only in this spec. The lesson is tiered 'both' and already uses higher-only blocks elsewhere, so the tip must say so. Practice Q3 cannot be tiered in its data shape, but it does supply the 1/d squared rule in the stem, so a Foundation student can still work it; its arithmetic recomputes correctly ((20/40) squared = 0.25; 30 x 0.25 = 7.5).
findings.evidence: spec 4.4.1.2 '(HT only) Students should understand and use inverse proportion - the inverse square law and light intensity in the context of photosynthesis'; recomputation of Q3

findings.claim: "An oxygen debt builds up - this is the extra oxygen needed after exercise to break down the accumulated lactic acid in the liver, where it is converted back to glucose." (outside any higher-only block)
findings.truth: The liver step and the definition of oxygen debt are Higher tier only; only 'creates an oxygen debt' is core. The same content is already correctly wrapped in higher-only further down the lesson (n28, n29), so trimming this sentence loses nothing for Higher students.
findings.evidence: spec 4.4.2.2 core vs '(HT only) Blood flowing through the muscles transports the lactic acid to the liver where it is converted back into glucose. Oxygen debt is the amount of extra oxygen...'

findings.claim: The whole of lesson 9: culturing microorganisms, nutrient broth and agar, aseptic technique, the 25 degC school incubation rule, the antibiotic / disinfectant 'required practical' with zones of inhibition, plant disease (TMV, rose black spot, aphids), plant disease detection, nitrate and magnesium ion deficiency, and plant defence responses.
findings.truth: None of this is in this qualification. The spec has no culturing, agar, aseptic technique, plant disease or plant defence content, and no microbiology required practical: 4.3 Infection and response runs 4.3.1.1 to 4.3.1.9 and stops at drug development. It is separate-biology content, and the lesson still points its diagram at the separate-sciences image path. Wrapping it in a higher-only block does not fix this - it is a qualification question, not a tier question. Options: (a) retire lessons 9 and 10 from this unit and leave them in the separate-sciences subject, which is where they already exist; (b) keep them as clearly labelled enrichment with every 'required practical' and 'in the exam' claim stripped; (c) if these pupils are actually entered for separate biology, move the whole unit. Recommendation: (a). The facts inside the lesson check out - binary fission every 20 minutes giving over 1 million after 7 hours (2^21 = 2,097,152), area = pi r squared worked examples (314 mm2, 283 mm2, 154 mm2, 113 mm2) and the 25 degC rule all recompute correctly - so nothing is lost by moving rather than rewriting.
findings.evidence: grep of the spec: no hit for culturing, agar, aseptic, petri, plant disease, monoclonal; spec 4.3.1.1-4.3.1.9; the qualification's biology required practicals are 1-5 only

findings.claim: The whole of lesson 10: monoclonal antibodies, hybridoma production, pregnancy testing, cancer treatment and the ethics of monoclonal antibody production.
findings.truth: Monoclonal antibodies do not appear anywhere in this qualification's spec; they are separate-biology content (the same 4.3.2 block as lesson 9). The lesson also points its diagram at the separate-sciences image path. Same decision as F17 and it should be taken together with it. Recommendation: retire from this unit. The biology inside the lesson is sound and Q3 recomputes correctly (750 x 0.048 = 36; 750 x 0.104 = 78; total 114).
findings.evidence: grep of the spec: no hit for monoclonal; spec 4.3.1.1-4.3.1.9

findings.claim: "In AQA Biology exams, questions on culturing microorganisms often ask you to describe the aseptic technique step by step..."
findings.truth: Names the board and tells the student this content is examined. It is not examined on this course (see F17). The teaching point is worth keeping; the exam claim and the board name are not.
findings.evidence: house rule; spec scope as F17

findings.claim: Card 4: q "_____ from one bacterium, this means there could be over 1 million bacteria after just 7 hours", a "Starting".
findings.truth: The answer is the word 'Starting'. Rebuilt as a zones-of-inhibition definition card from the lesson's own glossary.
findings.evidence: reading the card

findings.claim: "Once a lymphocyte becomes a B lymphocyte and starts producing antibodies, it loses the ability to divide."
findings.truth: A lymphocyte does not 'become a B lymphocyte' - it is already one. It is the antibody-producing cell it differentiates into that stops dividing. The sentence is trimmed to say that.
findings.evidence: settled fact; beyond GCSE detail either way

findings.claim: Card 5 answer (herd immunity) is 31 words.
findings.truth: The flashcard validator caps answers at 30 words, so the unit would fail validation once the other card edits land. Shortened to 22 words with the same meaning.
findings.evidence: validator limit in the checker brief; word count

findings.claim: "Without enough nitrate, the plant ... shows stunted growth and yellowing of older leaves (chlorosis)."
findings.truth: Botanically true, but it cuts across the lesson's own key fact and knowledge check, which pin yellow leaves to magnesium and stunted growth to nitrate. Not worth an edit while the lesson's place in this unit is unresolved (F17).
findings.evidence: lesson key fact n31 and knowledge check 2 vs n30

findings.claim: "In 2006, a clinical trial of the monoclonal antibody TGN1412 caused six healthy volunteers to suffer multiple organ failure within minutes."
findings.truth: 'Within minutes' is the standard textbook compression - reactions began within about an hour and a half and organ failure developed over the hours that followed. Not certain enough about the exam-board wording to correct it, and the lesson may be retired anyway (F18).
findings.evidence: settled only in outline; checker brief says record rather than correct when not certain

findings.claim: Lesson 9's slug is 'lesson-01' and lesson 10's is 'lesson-02', the same slugs as lessons 1 and 2 in this unit.
findings.truth: Two pairs of colliding slugs inside one unit. Not a content fact, but it is the fingerprint of the copy from the separate-sciences subject (see F17, F18) and it will break per-lesson routing. Flagging it for whoever takes the F17 decision.
findings.evidence: raw headers of L01, L02, L09, L10

summary: Two whole lessons (9 Culturing Microorganisms and Plant Disease, 10 Monoclonal Antibodies) are separate-biology content that this qualification does not carry, copied in from the separate-sciences subject - diagram paths and duplicate slugs included - and they need Tom's ruling, not an edit. Everything else is systematic: the required practical numbers follow the separate-biology spec (3, 5, 6 where this course uses 2, 4, 5), six places name the exam board, five flashcards are mangled auto-cloze cards with answers like 'Latestage', 'They', 'Starting' and a duplicated 'CO8322', and three smaller science errors - ultraviolet called ionising radiation, the Higher-only inverse square law and liver lactic-acid step taught unflagged, and an answer key accepting the wrong unit. All numeric worked examples, equations and knowledge check answer keys in the unit recompute correctly.
